title: Longest Subsequence With Non-Zero Bitwise XOR
summary: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subsequence with a non-zero bitwise XOR.
statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subsequence with a non-zero bitwise XOR. Return 0 if no such subsequence exists.
constraints: nums contains one to 100,000 nonnegative integers.
Choose a subsequence whose bitwise XOR is nonzero.
Return its maximum length, or zero when none exists.
known_wrong_solutions:
def longest_nonzero_xor_subsequence(nums):
    total=0
    for value in nums:total^=value
    if total:return len(nums)-1
    if all(value==0 for value in nums):return 0
    return len(nums)-1
def longest_nonzero_xor_subsequence(nums):
    total=0
    for value in nums:total^=value
    if total:return len(nums)
    if any(value==0 for value in nums):return 0
    return len(nums)-1
hints: First test the XOR of the complete array.
If it is zero but some value is nonzero, removing that value makes the remaining XOR equal that nonzero value.
Return n for nonzero total XOR, zero for an all-zero array, and n-1 otherwise.
No length n answer exists when the total XOR is zero, while the removal argument always constructs the optimal length n-1 answer.
editorial: No length n answer exists when the total XOR is zero, while the removal argument always constructs the optimal length n-1 answer.

tests.explanation: The full XOR is zero, but removing any nonzero value leaves a length-two valid subsequence.
The XOR of all three values is five, so all elements can be kept.
